text: What should not be claimed yet in the Morgan Street CIO demo?
claudePromptBoundary: Full production prompt is reconstructed from current source template and captured source packet. ai_egress_audit stores prompt hash/snapshot refs, not raw prompt text by default.
claudeResponse:
Lakeshore Holdings has real momentum to show in the Morgan Street CIO demo, but there are four categories of claims that would undermine credibility if made before the evidence is in hand. Don't claim specific value numbers.
The loaded evidence includes Finance's own note that pilot cycle-time improvement should be 8-12% and that outside counsel avoidance is directional — hard savings require Finance attestation. Any ROI figure, cost-avoidance dollar, or payback period stated as fact in the demo is premature. Don't claim HR or Legal are ready to scale.
Workday HR process volumes, CLM matter data, policy taxonomy, and legal control boundaries haven't been loaded. Showing those functions as active value-office workstreams rather than discovery branches overstates readiness. Don't claim ServiceNow deflection or resolution-quality outcomes. Ticket-volume baselines, repeat-contact drivers, and deflection measurement aren't yet validated.
The service desk use case can be described as shaped — not proven. Don't claim Treasury bank-connectivity proof is complete. Critical-bank certification evidence, payment exception cost baselines, and SOX signer attestation are all listed as missing. Kyriba cash visibility is the right proof-point direction; the closed-loop evidence isn't there yet.
What the demo can credibly show: a governance-ready, Finance/Treasury-anchored Phase 1 with named systems (Kyriba, Oracle Fusion, Workday Finance), named initiatives, and a value-office design that Finance has already pressure-tested on assumptions. That's a strong CIO story — it just needs to stay inside the evidence boundary.
